overview: Explore top accredited institutions, tuition costs, eligibility, and visa procedures in Sweden for Biomedical Engineering (PG) in Sweden.

universities.name: \. Chalmers University of Technology
universities.desc: Chalmers offers a two-year MSc programme in Biomedical Engineering, taught in English. The programme includes specialisation opportunities in areas such as Neuroengineering and Sensor Technology, AI in Healthcare, and Clinical Innovation and Implementation. Students can study medical devices, biomedical signals, imaging, artificial intelligence and digital healthcare technologies. **Location:** Gothenburg **![][image1]**

universities.name: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology
universities.location: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden
universities.desc: KTH offers a related MSc programme in Medical Engineering, which connects engineering methods with medical and healthcare applications. It may be suitable for students interested in medical technology, healthcare systems, instrumentation and engineering solutions to clinical challenges. **Location:** Stockholm **![][image2]** **Understanding the programme differences:** Chalmers offers a direct Biomedical Engineering programme, while KTH's Medical Engineering programme is a closely related alternative. Students should review the curriculum, specialisations and eligibility criteria before applying.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Biomedical Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Sweden.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Biomedical Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Swedish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Biomedical Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between SEK 80,000 and SEK 150,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students holding a valid Swedish residence permit for higher education are permitted to work alongside their studies without a fixed hours limitation during term time.
